colp.label: Report to City of London Police online
colp.note: For the Square Mile. You can also call 101.

btptext.label: Text British Transport Police
btptext.note: Discreet and non-emergency. The Text BTP tab helps you write the message.

ani.label: Ask for ANI at a participating pharmacy
ani.note: Say "ANI" to staff to get a private space and help to contact police or support.

actionfraud.label: Report fraud to Action Fraud
actionfraud.verify: This may now be the Report Fraud service.

actionfraudtel.label: Action Fraud by phone
actionfraudtel.verify: This may now be the Report Fraud service.

fixmystreet.label: Report on FixMyStreet
fixmystreet.note: It sends the report to the right council, or to TfL for red routes.

streetlink.label: Tell StreetLink
streetlink.note: StreetLink connects people sleeping rough to local outreach teams.

tfltaxi.label: TfL taxi and private hire information
tfltaxi.note: Use black cabs or pre-booked licensed minicabs only.

gas.label: National Gas Emergency Service
gas.note: 24/7. Get outside. Do not use switches or flames.

water.label: Thames Water (most of London)
water.note: Parts of outer London are served by Affinity Water, SES Water or Essex & Suffolk Water. Check your water bill to see which company is yours.

tfllost.label: TfL lost property
tfllost.verify: Check this page path still works.

staff.label: Tell station staff
staff.note: They can help at once with broken lifts and other station problems.

fsa.label: Food Standards Agency
fsa.note: Food problems go to the local council.

rogue.label: Rogue Landlord and Agent Checker (Mayor of London)

landlord.label: Tell your landlord in writing first
landlord.note: Keep a copy. If nothing happens, contact the council's private housing team.

venue.label: Tell venue staff or security straight away
venue.note: Then report to the police as soon as possible, because evidence fades fast.

categories.title: Harassment or crime on transport
include: What happened, in a few plain words
Where: line, station, bus route or number plate
When it happened
What the person looked like, if you can say
Carriage number if on a train (inside the doors or at the end)

options.label: Train, Tube, Overground, Elizabeth line, DLR or tram
On a bus or at a bus stop
A station problem, not a crime (lift, staff)

rail.who: British Transport Police handle crime and harassment on trains, Tube, Overground, Elizabeth line, DLR, trams and at stations.

bus.who: The Met handles crime on buses and at bus stops.

cab.who: The Met handles crime in taxis and minicabs. TfL licenses taxis and private hire vehicles.
include: Operator name and number plate
Time, pick-up and drop-off places
Booking details or app receipt, if you have them

station.who: TfL and station staff look after lifts, facilities and staff issues.
include: Station and line
What is wrong (for example, which lift)
When you noticed

categories.title: Theft or street crime
include: What was taken, with make, model or serial number
Where and when
What the person looked like, if you saw them
Any CCTV nearby you noticed
Block your phone and bank cards with your provider

options.label: On a train, Tube, tram or at a station
On a bus or at a bus stop
In the Square Mile (City of London)

rail.who: British Transport Police handle crime on trains, Tube, trams and at stations.

main.who: The Metropolitan Police handle crime across London, including on buses.

city.who: City of London Police cover the Square Mile.

categories.title: Hate incident
include: What was said or done, as exactly as you can
Where and when
Why you think you were targeted, in your words
Any witnesses, photos, video or screenshots
Descriptions of the people involved

options.label: Yes: train, Tube, Overground, Elizabeth line, DLR, tram or station

rail.who: British Transport Police handle hate crime on the rail network. You can also use True Vision online.

main.who: The police take hate incident reports. You can report online through True Vision, or call 101. Call 999 if you are in danger.

categories.title: Domestic abuse
include: You do not need to have everything. Say what you feel safe to share
Dates and what happened, if you want to keep a record
Keep any evidence somewhere safe and private

questions.text: Are you in danger right now?

options.label: No, I want help or advice

danger.who: Call 999. If you cannot speak, call from a mobile and stay on the line. When a recorded message asks, press 55 to be put through to the police.

advice.who: The National Domestic Abuse Helpline is free and open 24/7. Police take reports on 101, or 999 if you are in danger.

categories.title: Scam or fraud
include: How they contacted you and when
Amounts and how you paid
Phone numbers, websites or email addresses used
Screenshots and messages. Do not delete them

questions.text: Have you lost money or shared bank details?

options.label: No, I want to report a scam attempt

lost.who: Your bank can act fastest if you call now. Then report the fraud.

attempt.who: Forward scam texts and emails. Report fraud to Action Fraud.

categories.title: Street problem (potholes, lights, fly-tipping, graffiti)
include: Exact place: street name, nearest house number or a map pin
A clear photo
What is wrong and how long it has been like this

main.who: Your council looks after most streets. TfL looks after red routes. FixMyStreet sends your report to the right one.

categories.title: Noise or neighbours
include: Address or place the noise comes from
Days and times, and how long it lasts
A short log of dates. Note what you heard
What you have already tried, if anything

main.who: Your council deals with noise and nuisance neighbours. Antisocial behaviour can also go to the police on 101.

categories.title: Someone sleeping rough
include: Exact place, as precisely as you can
Time you saw them
A short description, so outreach can find them

main.who: StreetLink connects people sleeping rough to local outreach teams. If someone is in danger or needs medical help, call 999.

categories.title: Unsafe driving
include: Dashcam or helmet-cam footage, with date and time
Number plate, vehicle make and colour
Exact place and direction of travel
Keep the original video file

main.who: With dashcam or helmet-cam footage, you can report unsafe driving to the Met online.

categories.title: Unlicensed cab or tout
include: Number plate and car description
Place and time
What the person said or did
What the person looked like

main.who: Use black cabs or pre-booked licensed minicabs only. Report touting to the police on 101. TfL has information on taxis and private hire.

categories.title: Spiking
include: Where you were and when it happened
What you were drinking, and who was with you
Keep the drink or glass if you can
A trusted friend to stay with you

questions.text: Does someone feel unwell right now?

options.label: No, I want to report it

unwell.who: Call 999 and tell venue staff or security straight away. Stay with the person.

report.who: Report to the police as soon as possible, because evidence fades fast. Tell venue staff or security too.

categories.title: Mental health crisis
include: Where the person is and who is with them
Stay with them if it is safe to do so
Say what is happening in plain words

questions.text: Is a life in danger right now?

options.label: No, I need help or advice

advice.who: NHS 111 can help. Choose the mental health option. Samaritans listen, free, 24/7.

categories.title: Gas, water, power or flooding
include: Your address and what you can see, hear or smell
When it started
Your account number, if you have it

gas.who: The National Gas Emergency Service is free and 24/7. Get outside. Do not use switches or flames.

power.who: Call 105 to reach your local network operator. It is free.

water.who: Your water company handles leaks and no water. Most of London is Thames Water.

flood.who: Floodline gives flood advice. Call 999 if a life is at risk.

categories.title: Lost property
include: What it is, with colour, make and any marks
Where and when you lost it (line, station or bus route)
Your contact details

options.label: On TfL: Tube, bus, Overground, DLR, tram or Elizabeth line

tfl.who: TfL runs lost property for its services.

other.who: Ask the venue or operator where you lost it. If you think it was taken, report it to the police.

stolen.who: Report stolen property to the police.

categories.title: Child at risk
include: The child's name and age, if you know
Where they are, and what you saw or heard
Why you are worried, in plain words
Who else might know

questions.text: Is the child in immediate danger?

worried.who: The NSPCC helpline gives advice to anyone worried about a child. The council's children's services can also act.

categories.title: Exploitation or modern slavery
include: What you have seen or heard, and where
Names, addresses, vehicles or phone numbers, if known
Do not confront anyone. Your safety comes first

main.who: The Modern Slavery & Exploitation Helpline takes reports and gives advice. Call 999 if someone is in danger.

categories.title: Suspicious activity
include: What you saw, where and when
Descriptions of people and vehicles
Do not touch anything suspicious

questions.text: Are you on a train or at a station?

rail.who: On trains, text British Transport Police. Call 999 if it is immediate.

main.who: Call 999 if it is immediate. Otherwise use the Anti-Terrorist Hotline or report online.

categories.title: Animal welfare
include: Where the animal is and what you can see
How long you have seen this
Photos, if safe to take

main.who: The RSPCA takes animal welfare reports.

categories.title: Food hygiene
include: Business name and address
What you saw and when
Photos, if appropriate. Keep any receipt

main.who: Food hygiene problems go to the local council. The Food Standards Agency has more information.

categories.title: Housing disrepair
include: Photos and dates of each problem
Copies of messages and letters to your landlord
Your tenancy details
What you have already asked for

main.who: Tell your landlord in writing first. Then contact the council's private housing team.
